$comment: Agreed Estonian terminology for this project. Injected into every translation batch and checked against finished translations by `glossary-check`. Machine-proposed from the English corpus with Finnish (official EA translation) as reference, so treat every row as correctable: fix the Estonian, add `accept` alternatives rather than arguing with the checker. `accept` lists equally correct renderings; `note` says when a term means something else in another context; `caseSensitive` keeps a term that is also an ordinary word from matching prose; `ambiguous` marks a common English word that also has ordinary-language senses, so the checker only polices it in short labels and trusts the prompt to prevent drift in prose.

the owner's choice, 2026-10-17: Flirdi. The verb is flirtima and the action noun flirtimine (cf. Kiss -> Suudlemine) if the family style is wanted later. It was briefly 'Flirttaile', which is the Finnish word.

style: Buttons and menu entries are imperative verb phrases (Salvesta, Laadi, Välju), not nouns.
Do not attach Estonian case endings to runtime-inserted names or values; rephrase instead.
Keep English proper nouns that Estonian players know in English (Sim, The Sims 4) rather than inventing translations.
Prefer the glossary rendering over your own synonym, even when yours reads better in isolation: two screens disagreeing is worse than one screen being slightly stiff.

Moodlet sources, the 1,588 strings shaped "(From X)", are written "(X tõttu)": "(From Snob Trait)" -> "(snobi iseloomujoone tõttu)". The first batches split between this and "(põhjus: X)"; this is the agreed form.
Square brackets hold player-facing text, not codes: translate inside them, keeping the brackets ([Recovered] -> [Taastatud]). Only [PH] and [DNT] are development markers and stay as they are.

A reference language is for how a construct was handled, never for words: "flirttailla" and "vehtailu" are Finnish and were copied into the Estonian once each (Flirttaile, Vehtle). If a word is not one you would say, do not use it.
